y-m-05-02.title: How many ways to use all sticks?
y-m-05-02.topic: Number of sides in triangles and quadrilaterals
y-m-05-02.goal: Using stick counts for triangle and quadrilateral, find different ways to use all 31 sticks and describe rule for changing between solutions.
y-m-05-02.material: 31 same-length sticks dey. One triangle use 3 sticks; one quadrilateral use 4. Sticks for one shape no shared with another. Use all 31 with none left, and make at least 1 triangle and 1 quadrilateral.
y-m-05-02.thinking.0: Finding how many sticks each shape need
y-m-05-02.thinking.1: Making several ways wey fit conditions

y-m-05-02.s.s1.r.a: Dis na thinking wey find stick count for each shape, add dem, and compare with 31.
y-m-05-02.s.s1.o.b: All di sticks finish, nothing remain
y-m-05-02.s.s1.r.b: Dis na thinking wey only look number of shapes, like say 9 shapes dey altogether, or judge without checking number of sticks.
y-m-05-02.s.s1.r.c: Dis na thinking wey count sticks for triangle or quadrilateral wrong once. Count again for each shape.
y-m-05-02.s.s1.explain: 6 triangles need 18 sticks and 3 quadrilaterals need 12 sticks, so dem use 30 sticks altogether. If dem use 30 of di 31 sticks, 1 remain.
y-m-05-02.s.s2.prompt: Make t triangles and s quadrilaterals, then find three different ways to use all 31 sticks. (t and s each na natural number at least 1.)

y-m-05-02.s.s2.hint.1: Check how many quadrilaterals you fit make with di sticks wey remain, and whether any stick remain.

y-m-05-02.s.s2.fail.c1: Both triangle and quadrilateral numbers must be natural numbers at least 1.
y-m-05-02.s.s2.ok.c2: Use all 31 sticks without any remaining.
y-m-05-02.s.s2.fail.c2: Some sticks remain or dem no plenty. Add sticks wey triangles need and sticks wey quadrilaterals need, then check whether total na 31.
y-m-05-02.s.s2.explain: These ones possible: 9 triangles and 1 quadrilateral (27+4), 5 triangles and 4 quadrilaterals (15+16), 1 triangle and 7 quadrilaterals (3+28). If at least 1 of each dey, na only these three ways.
y-m-05-02.s.s2.because.prompt: After you find one way, explain how to quickly find another way while still using exactly 31 sticks.
y-m-05-02.s.s2.because.hint.0: Count how many sticks remain if you remove some triangles from di way wey you find.
y-m-05-02.s.s2.because.hint.1: Check how many more quadrilaterals you fit make with those sticks.
y-m-05-02.s.s2.because.selfAssess.0: You check again say di new way use 31 sticks too?
y-m-05-02.s.s2.because.selfAssess.1: You talk how di number of triangles and quadrilaterals dey swap with each other?
y-m-05-02.s.s2.because.model.0: If you remove 4 triangles, 12 sticks remain. You fit make 3 quadrilaterals with those sticks, so you fit change 4 triangles to 3 quadrilaterals.
y-m-05-02.s.s2.because.model.1: Remove triangles one by one and count how many quadrilaterals you gain from di sticks. 4 triangles and 3 quadrilaterals both use 12 sticks, so swapping dem keep total at 31.
y-m-05-02.s.s2.because.model.2: If you remove 4 triangles (12 sticks) and use those sticks to make 3 quadrilaterals, you still use all 31.

y-m-05-03.title: How many building blocks dey if na only di front we see?
y-m-05-03.goal: Realize say total number of building blocks no fit decide from front view alone, and find for yourself di information wey let you decide am and possible numbers.
y-m-05-03.material: Building blocks na wooden cubes of di same size. 3 spots dey side by side from left to right. For front row, left spot get 2 blocks (2 levels), middle spot get 1, and right spot get 1, so front row get 4 blocks altogether. From front, e look like stairs, with left side one level higher. Back row fit dey behind front row, but front row hide am, so you no fit see. If back row dey, each spot no stack higher than di same spot for front row (if e higher, you go see am from front). Blocks no dey float, and na only two rows dey, front and back.

y-m-05-06.title: Desk measured by hand spans: which one longer?
y-m-05-06.goal: Know measurements by different people's spans no compare by span count alone. Update judgment as info arrive, and make cases with equal lengths.
y-m-05-06.material: Gaeun and Narae each measure long side of desk using own hand span (thumb to little finger spread wide). Each person's span about same each time. Centimeter (cm) unit for length.
y-m-05-06.s.s1.prompt: Each time new info come, update which desk longer.
y-m-05-06.s.s1.hint.0: First check who measure and whether span length same standard.
y-m-05-06.s.s1.hint.1: With new info, see if desk lengths can show in same unit (cm).
y-m-05-06.s.s1.st.0.info: Desk 가 4 spans, desk 나 3. Gaeun measure both using her span.
y-m-05-06.s.s1.st.0.after: Same person use same span, so 4 spans longer than 3.
y-m-05-06.s.s1.st.0.r.a: This idea see same person same span mean more spans longer.
y-m-05-06.s.s1.st.0.r.b: This assumes fewer spans mean longer. Reconsider same-span case.
y-m-05-06.s.s1.st.0.r.c: This idea no use info same person measured both.
y-m-05-06.s.s1.st.1.info: Actually Gaeun measure desk 가, Narae desk 나, each own span. We don't know their span lengths.
y-m-05-06.s.s1.st.1.after: Different people use different span sizes, so count alone no guarantee. First guess may be right, but need span lengths to check.
y-m-05-06.s.s1.st.1.o.a: Desk 가 look longer, but unsure.
y-m-05-06.s.s1.st.1.r.a: This keep first guess but lower confidence.
y-m-05-06.s.s1.st.1.o.b: We can't tell. Don't know lengths of both spans.
y-m-05-06.s.s1.st.1.r.b: This recognizes measurements with different standards no compare directly.
y-m-05-06.s.s1.st.1.r.c: This flips initial judgment with new info but hard to explain why.
y-m-05-06.s.s1.st.2.ask: If show both desk lengths in cm and compare, what happen?
y-m-05-06.s.s1.st.2.after: Desk 가=9+9+9+9=36cm; desk 나=13+13+13=39cm. Even fewer spans, longer span may make desk longer.
y-m-05-06.s.s1.st.2.r.a: This idea estimate span-length difference equals span-count difference.
y-m-05-06.s.s1.st.2.r.b: This assumes more spans still mean longer.
y-m-05-06.s.s1.st.2.r.c: This finds each desk cm length and compare.
y-m-05-06.s.s1.reflect: With same person measuring, compare by span counts. Different people's spans no sure; compare only after know one span length in same unit (cm).

y-m-05-06.s.s2.because.prompt: Explain why desk lengths fit same even though span counts different, 4 and 3.

y-m-05-07.title: How count triangles in square without missing any?
y-m-05-07.goal: Compare methods to count big and small triangles without missing or double-counting; fix wrong count, and make method for another picture.
y-m-05-07.material: Start top-left and go clockwise: label square paper corners ㄱ,ㄴ,ㄷ,ㄹ. Draw straight lines ㄱ-ㄷ and ㄴ-ㄹ, meet center ㅁ. Count all big and small triangles. Each triangle side must lie on drawn lines. (ㄱ read giyeok, ㄴ nieun, ㄷ digeut, ㄹ rieul, ㅁ mieum.)
y-m-05-07.prereq.0: Know triangle enclosed by 3 straight lines (Grade 2)
y-m-05-07.s.s1.prompt: Four friends describe triangle counting. Choose methods count every triangle once.
y-m-05-07.s.s1.hint.0: For each method, imagine what triangles may be missed.
y-m-05-07.s.s1.hint.1: Check counted triangles distinguishable, no overlap.
y-m-05-07.s.s1.r.a: This misses big triangles made by two small ones.
y-m-05-07.s.s1.o.b: Daon: Count small triangles first, then ones made by joining two small ones
y-m-05-07.s.s1.r.b: This sort by size and count in order.
y-m-05-07.s.s1.o.c: Hajun: Choose 3 of 5 points at a time, skip three points on same straight line
y-m-05-07.s.s1.r.c: This count by point selections and exclude cases not forming triangle.
y-m-05-07.s.s1.r.d: No order or rule, so may miss or double count.
y-m-05-07.s.s1.explain: Counting by size in order, or selecting 3 points while excluding collinear triples, can count all. Counting only smallest or by eye can miss some.
y-m-05-07.s.s1.acc.0: Daon method can count all. Hajun method too.
y-m-05-07.s.s1.acc.1: Hajun method can count all. Daon too.
